payload.body:
Exam written at `client/test/sync-origin.test.ts` — eight tests, every leg titled with its leg letter and its Machine clause.

At BASE: 5 fail, 3 pass, and each failure reads as the absent implementation —
- leg (a) `typeof StoreData.readSyncOrigin` is `undefined`;
- leg (a)'s second test: `client/src/vite-env.d.ts` has no `__TINYAPP_SYNC__?: string`;
- leg (b) `typeof Config.syncUrl` is `undefined`;
- legs (b)+(c) the render dials `ws://localhost:9876/sync/todos` where the exam origin's URL is expected;
- leg (e) the Key Files section names only the seed and the exam flag.

The three that pass are leg (d)'s: BASE's unhandled page, seeded page and flagged page already behave as M4 requires them to keep behaving, so that leg is a standing control rather than a change.

Readings a later session would otherwise reconstruct:

1. Legs (b) and (c) are two halves of *one* render — unseeded, unflagged, handle set — so the file renders it once and asserts both. Splitting it into two renders would have asserted 'exactly once' about two different sockets.

2. The socket assertions are `expect(socketUrls).toEqual([EXAM_URL])` rather than a count plus a containment: the leg pins an exact URL and a count of one, and one array equality says both. `reconnecting-websocket` and the global `WebSocket` are stubbed with the same recording class, so a dial made either way lands in that array and a page that must dial nothing is held to `[]`.

3. Leg (c)'s 'equal to the Provider's store' is `toBe` against the store a probe component reads back out of the Provider under `STORE_ID` — object identity, not content equality — and the `setTodoCompleted` follow-up is the clause's own second half, checked by comparing the handle's full `getContent()` to the app store's.

4. Leg (a)'s window case saves `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, 'window')`, defines `window` as `undefined`, and restores in a `finally` — every later test needs the DOM back, so the restore cannot be conditional on the assertion passing.

5. Leg (e) is the Proof's first `Run:` line re-expressed in-file, using `client/test/seeded-store-global.test.ts`'s section slicer: `sed`'s inclusive range becomes a `findIndex` for `^## Key Files` and the next `^## Working Method`, `tr '\\n' ' '` becomes `join(' ')`, and `grep -q` becomes the same-ordered regex. The driver still runs the shell line; this is so the one exam file covers all five legs.

6. `readSyncOrigin` and `syncUrl` are reached through `await import(...)` rather than named static imports. A named static import of a missing export is a link error that takes the whole file down before leg (e) can run; this way each leg reports its own absence.

Checked both directions: red at BASE as above, and green — 8 pass, 42 expect() calls — against a throwaway implementation of M1–M5 written and then reverted, so the tree here carries the exam file and nothing else.

examiner, round 1: the exam goes at packages/tinyapp-exam/test/celld.test.ts, importing startCelld and examSurface from 'tinyapp-exam' (the package name, as M1 and M3 word it), and starting real celld runtimes against the repository's own server/ directory with serverDir: 'server' exactly as leg (a) spells it.

Measured at BASE before writing leg (d), on this sandbox's celld 0.5.0: the root names a module object only from the x-tinyapp-module header it sets on a /sync/<module> request. A fork's seed request carries no such header, so a transition from a facet no client has ever dialled arrives with module: ''. Measured: events + fork('todos','todos@y') alone gives {module:'',seq:1} and {module:'',seq:2}; with one raw WebSocket dialled at ws://.../sync/todos@y first, the same fork's seed transition arrives as {module:'todos@y',seq:2}. So leg (d)'s events sub-leg is written with that sync dial as its setup — the action asserted is still events(cb) then fork('todos','todos@y'), and the transition asserted is still the fork's seed. The server is not edited (global constraint), and nothing in the helper can supply a name the root never sent.

Done; all four Run lines and both Checks green, and I walked legs (a)-(e) by hand against real celld runtimes before committing.

One decision a later session would otherwise rediscover: leg (d) asks that a fork's transition arrive with module 'todos@y', and at BASE it cannot, because a module object learns its name only from the x-tinyapp-module header the root forwards on /sync/<name> — the root's exam verbs build a bare Request('http://facet/exam/...'), so /exam/events hands the harness module:''. Measured: fork alone delivers [{module:'',seq:1},{module:'',seq:1},{module:'',seq:2}]. The server is frozen by the global constraint, so examSurface.fork dials ws /sync/<to> once and hangs up before it seeds (a bare GET is answered with a 101 and Bun's fetch rejects UnrequestedUpgrade, so it is a WebSocket open-then-close, cached per name); after that the seed transition reads {module:'todos@y',seq:2} and every later one is named too. The two load-time transitions the facets fire on wake still arrive nameless and always will — an exam that asserts on the FIRST message rather than searching for a matching one would still be red. The clean fix is in server/index.ts (forward x-tinyapp-module from the exam verbs), which this task may not edit; filed as an out-of-FILES concern.

Also: examSurface exposes call(verb, query) on the same fetch path, for leg (d)'s '(surface as any).call("nope")' reading, and events(cb) returns a handle that is both {close()} and a thenable resolving once the socket is open, so 'events(cb)' and 'await events(cb)' both read and a fork straight afterwards cannot outrun the socket.

exam-1: the exam is written at packages/tinyapp-exam/test/celld.test.ts — 11 tests, legs (a)-(e).

State at BASE: 0 pass / 11 fail. Ten of the eleven read `tinyapp-exam exports no \`startCelld\` yet — the exam helper is unbuilt`; the eleventh is leg (e) finding server/test/celld.ts still present. Both are the absent implementation and nothing else.

Checked it is passable, not merely red: with a throwaway lift of server/test/celld.ts into src/celld.ts + src/surface.ts, server/test/celld.ts deleted and the two server tests re-pointed, the file is 11 pass / 0 fail in 4.8 s. That stand-in was then removed — the tree holds the exam file and nothing else (git diff against BASE is empty). The dry run was taken twice, once with startCelld resolving serverDir against process.cwd() and once against the workspace root, and once each with events() returning a promise and returning a plain handle, so none of those choices is graded.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. serverDir is passed as the literal 'server' leg (a) spells, not as an absolute path. Both readings of 'relative to the workspace root' then work: resolve(cwd, 'server') and join(ROOT, 'server') name the same directory, where an absolute argument would be mangled by the second. The file guards on it — a run from anywhere but the workspace root says so in one line instead of failing as a missing server.

2. argv and env (M1) are read through the probe-binary form leg (a) offers: a shell script named through CELLD_BIN that writes its argv, its CELLD_ESBUILD and CELLD_MAX_RSS_MB and its own pid into a file and exits. That is why startCelld grows no seam M1 does not name. The same stand-in shape carries leg (b): 'echo boom >&2; exit 3' and 'exec sleep 600'. The exec matters — the recorded pid is then the process startCelld spawned, so 'the script is no longer running' is read on that pid and not on a shell above it.

3. 'runs bun build-facets.ts in serverDir' is read by dating server/generated/facets.ts back to 2020 before the call and finding it rewritten after: build-facets.ts writes that file unconditionally.

4. Leg (b)'s 'the script is no longer running' makes the SIGTERM-on-timeout part of the contract, though M1's own sentence stops at the rejection. The exam grades the leg.

5. The four Run: lines: the first three are assertions in the file (the absent server/test/celld.ts, and "from 'tinyapp-exam'" in each of the two server tests). The fourth — bun test over those two server tests — is deliberately not run here: an exam proves its own claim and never runs another exam. It is the driver's Run: line.

6. Every temp copy a rejected start leaves behind is removed in afterAll from the path the stand-in recorded, and both runtimes are stopped (leg (c) stops one, afterAll the other). A full run leaves nothing under os.tmpdir().

exam-1: one clause of leg (d) is not satisfiable against the server as at BASE, and is handed back under `unsatisfiable` rather than traded for another action.

The clause: "events(cb) followed by fork('todos', 'todos@y') delivers to cb within 5 s a transition whose \`module\` is \`todos@y\`".

Why it cannot hold. The module a transition names is the facet's own #name (server/facets/todos.ts), and a facet learns that name from the x-tinyapp-module header the root sets when it forwards /sync/<module> (server/index.ts, the /sync/ branch). The root's exam verbs build fresh requests with no such header — #exam()'s fork does `this.#facet(to).fetch(new Request('http://facet/exam/seed', ...))` — so a facet reached only through /exam/* never learns its name and reports the empty string. examSurface cannot supply it either: M3 gives fork one fetch of <url>/exam/fork?from&to and no dial.

Measured on this tree at BASE against a real celld dev runtime, exam flag on, a fork from todos to todos@y over an open /exam/events socket:
  {"module":"","seq":1,"content":[{},{}],"at":...}
  {"module":"","seq":2,"content":[{},{}],"at":...}

The two server tests at BASE see real module names because their sessions dial /sync/<module> from client processes first; a harness that only forks does not.

This is a plan defect, not an implementation defect, and the global constraint says the server is not this task's to edit — so the exam neither edits the root nor substitutes a sync dial the leg does not name. What the exam does grade of that leg, live: a transition delivered inside 5 s of the fork, its seq a number, every message parsed as {module, seq, content, at} with module a string, content a two-element snapshot, at a number, and close() resolving after. The exam does not assert module === '' either — pinning the defect as the contract would be the same mistake in the other direction.

Two ways out for whoever settles it: either the leg is rewritten to expect the transition the surface can actually produce, or a later task gives the root's exam verbs the x-tinyapp-module header they do not set (a server change, so a different task's scope).
